what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Guatemala in the United States: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 132300 Guatemalan asylum seekers in the United States, 95.6% of all asylum seekers from Guatemala.
Refugees from Guatemala, a separate group, live mostly in the United States and Mexico.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Guatemala in 1995, with the URNG.
The fact pack records no armed conflict in the later years, so it does not say why the number of asylum seekers grew again.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2000 at 101646 asylum seekers, and the figure then fell to a low in 2010.
It rose again from the late 2010s and reached its highest point, 184014, at the end of 2024.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2000 to 2002 and 2019 to 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the United States.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for the United States only.
